seo.title: Homeless help in Cardiff - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people who are homeless or at risk in Cardiff: emergency housing, outreach, food, health care, benefits, work and specialist support.

page.heading: Cardiff homeless and housing-crisis help
page.urgent: Immediate danger, serious illness, police, fire or ambulance: 999 or 112 Nowhere safe tonight or homeless: Cardiff Housing Options 029 2057 0750; outside office hours 029 2087 3141 Sleeping outside or concerned about someone who is: Outreach Services 029 2057 0715, 7am–7pm daily Urgent but not life-threatening medical help: NHS Wales 111; press 2 for urgent mental-health support
page.notice: Beds, meals, opening times and eligibility can change. Call before travelling when possible. An assessment, application, referral or outreach contact does not guarantee accommodation or another service. Never pay anyone who claims they can secure a council or charity place.
page.intro:
Tell the worker where you are tonight, where you usually sleep, your age, whether children are with you, and whether pregnancy, disability, illness, domestic abuse, immigration restrictions or a pet affects what is safe. Ask for Welsh-language support or an interpreter if needed.
Start here: call Housing Options and say clearly that you are homeless today or at risk of losing your home. Ask to make a homelessness application. If you have nowhere tonight, call the out-of-hours number after the daytime service closes. Temporary accommodation depends on an assessment.
page.footer: No Home Help does not provide emergency services or guarantee accommodation. Use nohomehelp.com. — https://nohomehelp.com/

entries.title: Emergency services
entries.description:
Phone: 999 or 112.
Call for immediate violence, serious injury, overdose, breathing difficulty, loss of consciousness, fire or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location or nearest landmark first. If you cannot speak on a mobile call to police, listen and press 55 when prompted.
NHS Wales emergency guidance

entries.title: Cardiff Housing Options
entries.description:
Phone: 029 2057 0750; email: HousingOptionsCentre@cardiff.gov.uk. The published service hours are Monday, Tuesday and Friday 9am–4:30pm, and Wednesday and Thursday 10am–4:30pm. You can also ask at a Cardiff Hub. — mailto:HousingOptionsCentre@cardiff.gov.uk
Say that you want to make a homelessness application. Explain children, pregnancy, disability, illness, care history, domestic abuse or another reason you may be vulnerable. Outside office hours call 029 2087 3141. Emergency accommodation is assessed and not guaranteed.
Council help when homeless now

entries.title: Cardiff Outreach Services
entries.description:
Phone: 029 2057 0715, 7am–7pm every day; email: HANR.Outreach@cardiff.gov.uk. — mailto:HANR.Outreach@cardiff.gov.uk
For people sleeping outside and for reports about a known location. The team can help with a homelessness application, accommodation routes, health, benefits, substance-use and mental-health services. Give the exact sleeping place and usual time. Contact does not guarantee that someone will be found or housed that day.
Council rough-sleeping help

entries.title: StreetLink and text report
entries.description:
Send a StreetLink alert or text REALCHANGE to 80800 with the location and description of an adult sleeping outside. Reports go to local outreach; neither service is an emergency line or bed-booking service. Call 999 for immediate danger or a child at risk. — sms:80800
Send a StreetLink alert | Huggard guidance — https://www.huggard.org.uk/get-help/

entries.title: The Wallich Rough Sleepers Intervention Team
entries.description:
The team works daily from 7am–3pm and checks known rough-sleeping locations. It can provide breakfast, hot drinks, sleeping bags, warm clothing and toiletries, plus housing, health, benefits and substance-use referrals.
Cardiff Rough Sleeping Services
entries.address: Base: 3 Pendyris Street, Cardiff CF11 6RJ

entries.title: Evening outreach and severe weather
entries.description:
Salvation Army outreach normally operates 5pm–9pm daily with food, hot drinks, emergency care and access routes to accommodation. When the Severe Weather Emergency Protocol is active, call Outreach on 029 2057 0715 for extra provision.
Council outreach and cold-weather information

entries.title: Unsafe home or domestic abuse
entries.description:
Call 999 in immediate danger. RISE: 029 2046 0566, 24 hours. Live Fear Free: 0808 8010 800, free and bilingual, 24 hours.
RISE can help all genders with safety planning and practical help; refuge or another safe place depends on assessment and availability. Do not return for papers or belongings if it is unsafe.
Cardiff domestic-abuse support

categories.title: Day centres, shelter pathways and housing support

entries.title: Huggard Day Centre
entries.description:
Open daily 8:30am–6pm for adults needing food, warmth or a safe space. Services include advice, free and low-cost meals, clothing, showers and laundry. Emergency beds are allocated by referral; visiting the day centre does not guarantee a bed.
How to get help | Huggard contact — https://www.huggard.org.uk/contact/
entries.address: Address: Huggard Buildings, Hansen Street, Cardiff CF10 5DW; use CF10 5JZ for sat nav

entries.title: The Wallich Solutions Service
entries.description:
Monday–Friday 8:30am–10am by appointment and 10am–3pm as a drop-in. For adults experiencing homelessness. Housing and benefits advice, support to secure or maintain accommodation, mental-health and substance-use referrals, showers, laundry, practical supplies, training and learning.
Email: CardiffSolutionService@thewallich.net. A separate council page lists 029 2066 8464 for the service. — mailto:CardiffSolutionService@thewallich.net
Wallich Cardiff services
entries.address: Address: 3 Pendyris Street, Cardiff CF11 6RJ

entries.title: Reconnection Service
entries.description:
Phone: 029 2057 0704; email: Reconnection@cardiff.gov.uk. Open Monday–Thursday 9am–4:30pm and Friday 9am–4pm, without appointment. — mailto:Reconnection@cardiff.gov.uk
For people who do not have a local connection to Cardiff, the service explores a safe return or another positive accommodation route. It should not replace an urgent homelessness application when you have nowhere safe.
Council partner services
entries.address: Address: Central Library Hub, The Hayes, Cardiff CF10 1FL

entries.title: Floating Support Team
entries.description:
Phone: 029 2053 7342; email: floatingsupportteam@cardiff.gov.uk. — mailto:floatingsupportteam@cardiff.gov.uk
Housing-related support for eligible Cardiff residents aged 16+ who are at risk of homelessness or starting a tenancy and face an additional barrier. A social worker, housing officer, health professional or Hub officer must refer you; self-referrals are not accepted.
Floating-support criteria

entries.title: Street Pastors
entries.description:
Phone: 07765 112400; email: info@streetpastors.org.uk. Volunteers normally work in the city centre Friday and Saturday 10pm–4am. — mailto:info@streetpastors.org.uk
They can listen, help people reach clothing, hostel and housing services, and sometimes accompany someone to an appointment. They are not an emergency accommodation provider.
Council description of partner help

entries.title: Huggard Day Centre
entries.description:
Anyone in need of food, warmth or a safe space can attend daily 8:30am–6pm. Free and low-cost meals are available; ask on arrival what is being served and whether capacity is limited.
Huggard access information
entries.address: Address: Huggard Buildings, Hansen Street, Cardiff CF10 5DW

entries.title: FoodCycle Cardiff Ely
entries.description:
A free, meat-free community meal is normally served Monday at 6:30pm. Everyone is welcome and no voucher or referral is normally needed. Children must be accompanied by an adult.
FoodCycle Wales meals
entries.address: Address: The Dusty Forge, 460 Cowbridge Road West, Ely, Cardiff CF5 5BZ

entries.title: FoodCycle Cardiff Riverside
entries.description:
A free, meat-free community meal is normally served Wednesday at 6:30pm. Everyone is welcome and no voucher or referral is normally required.
FoodCycle Cardiff locations
entries.address: Address: Wyndham Street Centre, 3–5 Wyndham Street, Riverside, Cardiff CF11 6DQ

entries.title: Cardiff Foodbank
entries.description:
Phone: 029 2048 4120. A referral agency must issue a voucher or code before collection. Cardiff Hubs, Money Advice and some health, housing and support workers can assess a referral.
Eight distribution centres operate on different days, including City Church, Woodville Christian Centre, Grangetown Baptist Church and St Saviour's Church. Do not go to the Titan Road warehouse for food; it does not distribute parcels.
Current centres and opening times

entries.title: Emergency food voucher and city food map
entries.description:
Call Cardiff Money Advice on 029 2087 1071 or visit a Hub. Staff may issue an emergency food voucher after assessment. The council's live map lists foodbanks, pantries and community fridges; rules and stock vary.
Council food and warm-space help

entries.title: Oasis Cardiff: sanctuary seekers
entries.description:
Phone: 029 2046 0424. Oasis provides a free weekday lunch and drop-in advice, classes and activities for asylum seekers and refugees. Confirm the day's programme before a long journey.
Oasis services
entries.address: Address: 69B Splott Road, Cardiff CF24 2BW

entries.title: Trinity Centre / Canolfan y Drindod
entries.description:
Phone: 029 2132 1120. This Methodist outreach centre hosts a free weekly Welcome Table lunch for everyone, a monthly women-only lunch, and refugee and asylum-seeker groups. Check the current programme before attending.
Trinity Centre sessions
entries.address: Address: Four Elms Road, Piercefield Place, Cardiff CF24 1LE

entries.title: Salvation Army evening outreach
entries.description:
Council-arranged evening outreach normally runs 5pm–9pm daily, offering food, hot drinks, emergency care and routes into services. The team moves around the city, so contact Cardiff Outreach on 029 2057 0715 for current access.
Cardiff outreach information

entries.title: Huggard showers, laundry and clothing
entries.description:
The day centre is open daily 8:30am–6pm and offers showers, laundry facilities and free clothing alongside food and advice. Ask about that day's access and waiting time.
Huggard practical help
entries.address: Address: Huggard Buildings, Hansen Street, Cardiff CF10 5DW

entries.title: The Wallich Solutions Service
entries.description:
Weekday drop-in access normally runs 10am–3pm. Ask about showers, laundry and practical provisions. Morning access before 10am is by appointment.
Wallich facilities
entries.address: Address: 3 Pendyris Street, Cardiff CF11 6RJ

entries.title: Trinity Toiletries Bank: asylum seekers
entries.description:
Asylum seekers in need can normally collect toiletries Wednesday 9am–2:30pm without booking. Bring a bag. Email: enquiries@trinitycentre.wales. — mailto:enquiries@trinitycentre.wales
Toiletries Bank
entries.address: Address: Trinity Centre, Four Elms Road, Piercefield Place, Cardiff CF24 1LE

entries.title: The Wallich Welfare Vehicle
entries.description:
The mobile vehicle can provide a shower, dryer, Wi-Fi, medical room and private support space when deployed in Cardiff or elsewhere in Wales. It has no fixed Cardiff schedule. Email welfarevehicle@thewallich.net or call 029 2066 8464 to ask where it is operating. — mailto:welfarevehicle@thewallich.net
Wallich Mobile Operations

entries.title: NHS urgent care
entries.description:
Emergency: 999. Urgent but not life-threatening: 111, free 24 hours. Tell the call handler if you have no fixed address, phone, transport or safe place to recover. BSL users can contact NHS 111 Wales through SignVideo.
Calling NHS 111 Wales

entries.title: Cardiff and Vale Health Inclusion Service
entries.description:
Walk-in homeless-outreach clinics are for people who live in hostels, use day services or sleep outside. No appointment is required. Ask hostel or day-centre staff for current clinic times, or ask Cardiff Outreach on 029 2057 0715.
Clinics can include nursing, GP assessment, health checks, vaccination, sexual and reproductive health, eye care and dental referrals. Times and locations change with outreach demand.
NHS homeless outreach clinics

entries.title: Register with a GP without an address or ID
entries.description:
Anyone can register with a GP practice in Wales. A fixed address and identification are not required. Prescriptions are free for people registered with a GP in Wales, and a free interpreter can be requested.
A practice may refuse only if its list is full or you live outside its area. Ask for an explanation if refused and call NHS Wales Shared Services on 02921 501500 for Contractor Services if you cannot find a practice.
NHS Cardiff GP registration rules

entries.title: Urgent dental care
entries.description:
Cardiff and Vale Dental Helpline: 0300 10 20 247, 24 hours. A clinician assesses the problem and, when appropriate, books an emergency clinic. Call 999 for severe swelling affecting breathing or swallowing, uncontrollable bleeding or major facial injury.
NHS Wales dental helplines

entries.title: Urgent mental-health support
entries.description:
Call NHS 111 and press 2 for urgent mental-health advice and support. Call 999 if life is in immediate danger. Samaritans: 116 123, free at any time.
Cardiff and Vale mental-health services

entries.title: Cardiff Homeless Multidisciplinary Team
entries.description:
For single adults accessing homelessness services. The team can provide rapid assessment and support involving mental-health workers, substance-use specialists, nursing, counselling, occupational therapy, dietetics, social work, women's specialists and employment support.
Ask Housing Options, Outreach, Huggard or The Wallich for access. This is not a public emergency department.
Council health and multidisciplinary support
entries.address: Assessment Centre: 32 Cowbridge Road East, Cardiff

entries.title: Cardiff Alcohol and Drug Team
entries.description:
Phone: 029 2078 8300. CADT provides practical guidance, needs assessment, community-care advice and one-to-one counselling for people affected by alcohol or drug use.
Council alcohol and drug support

entries.title: CAVDAS homelessness outreach and rapid prescribing
entries.description:
Cardiff and Vale Drug and Alcohol Service works with the council's homeless multidisciplinary team. Support includes outreach, counselling, harm reduction, take-home naloxone, blood-borne-virus and sexual-health screening, and rapid access to opioid-substitution prescribing for eligible people.
Ask an outreach or homelessness worker for access. Prescribing requires clinical assessment.
CAVDAS outreach services

categories.title: Toilets, internet, charging and warm spaces

entries.title: Central Library Hub / Hyb y Llyfrgell Ganolog
entries.description:
Free Wi-Fi, public computers, telephones, document scanning, library services and a reading and relaxation area. The Hub also hosts Money Advice, Into Work, Citizens Advice and council services on scheduled days.
Check the live Hub page for opening hours and appointment requirements. Printing and photocopying may cost.
Cardiff Hubs and libraries
entries.address: Address: The Hayes, Cardiff CF10 1FL

entries.title: Cardiff libraries
entries.description:
Libraries offer free Wi-Fi except at Tongwynlais, free public computers at listed branches and public printing. A library card and PIN are needed to log into a computer; ask staff how to join if you have no fixed address or identification.
Library computer and internet access

entries.title: Public toilets at Hubs
entries.description:
Cardiff Hubs have publicly available toilets, and visitors are welcome to use them without accessing another service. The council also lists public and Community Toilet Scheme locations. Check accessibility and current opening times before a long journey.
Cardiff toilet information | Hub locations — https://cardiffhubs.co.uk/

entries.title: Warm spaces
entries.description:
Cardiff Hubs and partner venues provide free warm places, company and access to advice during cold periods. Locations and seasonal opening times change.
Council warm-space and food support

entries.title: Cardiff Bus
entries.description:
Customer service: 029 2066 6444, Monday–Friday 7am–6pm. Use the official site for routes, timetables, fares and live disruption. Different operators may require different tickets.
Cardiff Bus contact

entries.title: Transport for Wales
entries.description:
Use the official journey planner for trains and participating bus routes. Ask a housing, health, council or Jobcentre worker before an essential appointment whether travel can be authorised; help is not automatic.
Transport for Wales

entries.title: Travel for interviews or a new job
entries.description:
Cardiff Into Work may help eligible jobseekers with travel and other work costs. Ask and obtain approval before paying. A Jobcentre work coach may separately consider agreed employment costs.
Into Work support

entries.title: Cardiff Airport
entries.description:
An integrated ticket connects a Transport for Wales train from Cardiff Central to Rhoose Cardiff International Airport station and the 905 bus to the terminal. Current total journey time is about 48 minutes. Check the day's timetable, connection and fare before travel; the airport is not a shelter.
Transport for Wales airport route

entries.title: Taking an animal on Cardiff Bus
entries.description:
Assistance dogs travel when space is available. One well-behaved dog or small animal may travel at the driver's discretion, under control and off the seats. Ask before boarding; transport permission does not mean accommodation will accept the animal.
Cardiff Bus animal rules

entries.title: Discretionary Assistance Fund for Wales
entries.description:
An Emergency Assistance Payment may help an eligible person aged 16+ in extreme hardship with food, gas, electricity, clothing or emergency travel after an unexpected crisis. It is a grant, not a loan. Apply online or call 0800 859 5924.
You must live in Wales and have no other money available. Limits apply to repeat awards, and ongoing bills are not covered. A decision or payment is not guaranteed immediately.
DAF eligibility | apply — https://www.gov.wales/discretionary-assistance-fund-daf/how-apply

entries.title: Cardiff Money Advice
entries.description:
Phone: 029 2087 1071. Free help with budgeting, income maximisation, benefits and debt. The team or a Hub may also assess emergency food vouchers and help with a DAF application.
Cardiff advice services

entries.title: Universal Credit without a fixed address
entries.description:
You can claim while rough sleeping, sofa surfing or staying in a hostel. With permission, use a trusted person's, hostel, day-centre or Jobcentre address. If you lack identification, a bank account, phone, email or National Insurance number, say so: alternatives may be possible.
Tell your work coach about homelessness, mental ill health or recovery needs and ask whether the claimant commitment should change temporarily. Supported or temporary accommodation may use Housing Benefit separately.
Universal Credit guidance for homeless people

entries.title: Benefits and council services at a Hub
entries.description:
Hubs can help with Housing Benefit, council tax, the housing waiting list, online applications and document scanning. Service days and appointment rules vary. Central Library Hub and several neighbourhood Hubs also host Money Advice and Into Work.
Find a Cardiff Hub

categories.title: Work, training and travel to an interview

entries.title: Into Work Advice Service
entries.description:
Free help with CVs, applications, job search, interviews, Universal Credit, skills training, volunteering and placements. Eligible people may receive help with childcare, travel or other work costs. Ask at Central Library Hub or another participating Hub.
Confirm funding before buying anything; support is assessed and not automatic.
Into Work support | Hub locations — https://cardiffhubs.co.uk/

entries.title: The Wallich training and development
entries.description:
The weekday Solutions Service offers access to training, learning and development alongside housing and welfare support. Drop-in normally runs 10am–3pm; morning access is by appointment.
Wallich Solutions Service
entries.address: Address: 3 Pendyris Street, Cardiff CF11 6RJ

entries.title: Huggard support and development
entries.description:
Adults using the day centre can ask about support, advice and development opportunities alongside immediate practical help. Attendance does not create a job or housing placement.
Huggard support
entries.address: Address: Huggard Buildings, Hansen Street, Cardiff CF10 5DW

entries.title: Find vacancies and a Jobcentre
entries.description:
Use the official Find a Job service and postcode search for a current Jobcentre. A Jobcentre can help with Universal Credit, work-coach appointments and National Insurance questions.
Find a Job | find a Jobcentre — https://find-your-nearest-jobcentre.dwp.gov.uk/

entries.title: Careers Wales
entries.description:
Free careers information and guidance for people in Wales, including job search, training, qualifications, CVs and interviews. Ask for telephone or online help if travel is difficult.
Careers Wales

categories.title: Housing law, debt and legal advice

entries.title: Shelter Cymru
entries.description:
Urgent housing helpline: 08000 495 495, Monday–Friday 9am–4pm; email: emailadvice@sheltercymru.org.uk. — mailto:emailadvice@sheltercymru.org.uk
Free, independent advice about homelessness, eviction, rent or mortgage arrears, disrepair and housing rights in Wales. Shelter Cymru does not operate accommodation, kitchens or emergency beds.
Shelter Cymru contact options

entries.title: Cardiff Advice Service
entries.description:
Citizens Advice and Speakeasy provide free, independent and confidential advice through Cardiff Hubs on benefits, debt, housing, employment, immigration, discrimination, family and consumer problems. Locations and opening times vary.
Council advice-service directory | find a Hub — https://cardiffhubs.co.uk/

entries.title: Speakeasy Law Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 029 2045 3111; email: info@speakeasy.cymru. Office open Monday–Friday 10am–1pm; most contact is by phone or email, with some face-to-face appointments. — mailto:info@speakeasy.cymru
Free specialist advice on homelessness, eviction, disrepair, benefits, debt and employment law for Cardiff and Vale residents. The team normally aims to connect a caller with an adviser within two working days.
Speakeasy Law Centre

entries.title: Housing prevention and landlord problems
entries.description:
Contact Housing Options before leaving a tenancy. The council can discuss rent arrears, debt, landlord relations, deposits, rent in advance and alternatives. In most cases a private renter has the right to remain until the legal process reaches a court bailiff warrant.
Council homeless-prevention help

entries.title: Civil Legal Advice and possession court
entries.description:
Phone: 0345 345 4345, Monday–Friday 9am–8pm and Saturday 9am–12:30pm. Legal Aid may cover eligible housing, debt, discrimination and domestic-abuse problems.
If facing possession, attend the hearing and ask court staff about the free Housing Loss Prevention Advice Service. Do not miss court while waiting for another appointment.
Civil Legal Advice | possession advice and court duty — https://www.gov.uk/guidance/legal-aid-for-possession-proceedings

entries.title: Care-of mail at Huggard
entries.description:
Huggard states that people believed to use its services may receive mail care of the centre. Ask first about permission, the exact address format, collection rules and how long post is kept. The centre cannot confirm to another person whether someone uses the service.
Do not send post or leave identification, papers or belongings without explicit permission.
Huggard mail information

entries.title: National Insurance number
entries.description:
Check old payslips, benefit letters, a tax account or UKVI account first. You may start work before receiving a number if you can prove the right to work, and do not need one to start a benefit claim.
Apply for or find a number

entries.title: Prove the right to work
entries.description:
British and Irish citizens may use an eligible passport or a birth or adoption certificate together with an official document showing the National Insurance number. Other people may use a share code or eligible immigration documents.
Do not pay an unofficial agent. Ask Cardiff Advice Service or a regulated adviser if status is unclear.
Official right-to-work service

entries.title: Replace a birth certificate or get passport advice
entries.description:
Order certificates through the General Register Office or relevant register office; fees apply. Contact HM Passport Office before paying if documents, referees or delivery are difficult. A charity may help with an application but cannot guarantee the fee.
Order a certificate | Passport Adviceline — https://www.gov.uk/passport-advice-line

entries.title: Scanning, printing and storage
entries.description:
Central Library Hub and neighbourhood Hubs provide computers, scanning and public telephones; printing may cost. No verified open-access public luggage-storage service was found. Ask Housing Options, Huggard or The Wallich about a safe option before leaving belongings.
Cardiff Hubs

entries.title: Migrant Help asylum helpline
entries.description:
Freephone: 0808 801 0503, Monday–Friday 8am–8pm, with emergency support at any time. Help with asylum support, destitution, accommodation problems and finding legal representation. Migrant Help is not a law firm.
GOV.UK asylum helplines

entries.title: Welsh Refugee Council
entries.description:
Phone: 0808 196 7273, normally 10am–2pm. Help for asylum seekers and newly recognised refugees can include housing, Universal Credit, Child Benefit and asylum-support applications. Ask for an interpreter if needed.
Welsh Refugee Council

entries.title: Oasis Cardiff
entries.description:
Phone: 029 2046 0424. Free weekday drop-in support for asylum seekers and refugees, including advice, advocacy, a daily lunch, English and Welsh classes, women-only and family sessions, wellbeing and social activities.
Oasis services
entries.address: Address: 69B Splott Road, Cardiff CF24 2BW

entries.title: Trinity Centre and Space4U
entries.description:
Phone: 029 2132 1120. Trinity hosts refugee and asylum-seeker support. Space4U normally meets Monday and Thursday afternoons with friendship, practical information, English classes, refreshments and a hot meal.
Trinity partners and sessions
entries.address: Address: Four Elms Road, Piercefield Place, Cardiff CF24 1LE

entries.title: Asylum Justice
entries.description:
Phone: 029 2049 9421. Free legal help for asylum seekers. Check access before attending because clinics and capacity can change.
NHS directory of asylum support
entries.address: Address: 113–116 Bute Street, Cardiff CF10 5EQ

entries.title: British Red Cross health-inclusion support
entries.description:
Phone: 01633 720000, option 2. For asylum-seeking, refugee and vulnerable migrant patients needing help to register with a GP, access dental care, pharmacies and statutory or community services.
NHS migrant-support directory
entries.address: Address: Cardiff Royal Infirmary, Longcross Street, Cardiff CF24 0SZ

entries.title: Modern Slavery and Exploitation Helpline
entries.description:
Call 08000 121 700 for confidential guidance if someone is controlled, threatened, forced to work or have sex, has pay or documents withheld, or cannot leave. Call 999 for immediate danger.
Modern Slavery Helpline

entries.title: RISE Cardiff
entries.description:
24-hour phone: 029 2046 0566; email: risereferrals@llamau.org.uk. — mailto:risereferrals@llamau.org.uk
Specialist support concerning domestic abuse, sexual violence, stalking, exploitation, trafficking, forced marriage and honour-based abuse. RISE can help with safety, securing a current home or finding another safe place. Refuge is subject to assessment and availability.
Cardiff domestic-abuse services

entries.title: Domestic-abuse help for men and national support
entries.description:
Dyn Wales for men: 0808 801 0321; email: dyn@saferwales.com. Live Fear Free for everyone: 0808 8010 800, free, bilingual and open 24 hours. — mailto:dyn@saferwales.com
Call 999 in immediate danger. Ask Housing Options for emergency housing as well as contacting a specialist service.
Council safe-housing information

entries.title: Young people: Llamau and Shelter Cymru
entries.description:
Daytime housing advice: 08000 495 495. Night and weekend Youth Homeless Helpline: 0800 328 0292, 5pm–9am Monday–Thursday and from 5pm Friday to 9am Monday.
For people up to age 25 needing advice and access to safe temporary accommodation. A call does not guarantee a placement. Contact Housing Options as well and state your age immediately.
Emergency help for young people

entries.title: Children under 18 and care leavers
entries.description:
Call 999 if a child is in immediate danger. Outside normal hours, Cardiff's Social Services Emergency Duty Team is 029 2078 8570. Tell Housing Options if you are under 18 or a care leaver and contact your social worker or personal adviser.
Sofa surfing still counts as homelessness. Do not send a child to an adult day centre alone.
Council emergency contacts

entries.title: Umbrella Cymru: LGBTQ+ support
entries.description:
Phone: 0300 302 3670; text: 07520 645700; email: info@umbrellacymru.co.uk. — sms:+447520645700 — mailto:info@umbrellacymru.co.uk
Specialist gender and sexual-diversity support across Wales, including discrimination, hate crime, unsafe relationships, homelessness, accommodation and changing identity documents. It is not emergency accommodation.
Umbrella Cymru support

entries.title: Veterans support
entries.description:
Cardiff Veterans Team: 029 2087 1071 for housing, employment, benefits and debt. Royal British Legion: 0808 802 8080. Change Step: 0300 777 2259 for veteran peer support.
Veterans at risk can also call Op FORTITUDE on 0800 952 0774. Accommodation is individually assessed.
Cardiff veteran support | national veteran housing route — https://www.gov.uk/guidance/getting-homelessness-support-as-a-veteran

entries.title: Age Cymru Advice
entries.description:
Phone: 0300 303 4498, Monday–Friday 9am–4pm; email: advice@agecymru.org.uk. — mailto:advice@agecymru.org.uk
Free, confidential advice for older people, their families and carers concerning benefits, housing, health, care and local services.
Age Cymru Advice

entries.title: Adult social care and safeguarding
entries.description:
Phone: 029 2023 4234. Ask for an assessment if disability, age, chronic illness, mental-health difficulty or substance dependence affects daily living, safety or independence. For an emergency outside hours call 029 2078 8570.
Social care does not replace a homelessness application. Contact both services when care needs affect safe accommodation.
Access adult-care services

entries.title: StreetVet
entries.description:
People experiencing homelessness can use the UK help form to ask about free volunteer veterinary care. Eligibility and local coverage are assessed. StreetVet is not an emergency service and does not cover existing bills or provide fostering.
Request StreetVet help

entries.title: Dogs Trust Together Through Homelessness
entries.description:
The UK-wide scheme helps eligible dog owners with veterinary costs and finding dog-friendly services. A participating homelessness service may need to apply. Assessment applies; existing bills and every procedure are not automatically covered.
Together Through Homelessness

entries.title: Tell every service about your pet
entries.description:
Tell Housing Options and each referrer the species, size, health, behaviour and vaccination status. Ask about pet-friendly accommodation or temporary animal care before accepting or rejecting an offer. Do not abandon an animal or arrive at a hostel expecting admission.
Search dog-friendly services

entries.title: Keep this page accurate
entries.description:
Services change. Please report a closed service, wrong detail or safer alternative through the project repository. Do not send private medical, immigration or housing documents.
How to contribute | report an issue — ../../CONTRIBUTING.md
